content.message:
My recommendation is the $649.95 Breville Barista Express Impress: one machine for grinding beans, brewing espresso and manually steaming milk. The matched Whole Latte Love page supports an integrated conical burr grinder with 25 settings, PID temperature control and a manual steam wand. Those features offer useful control as you learn. Expect to adjust the grind and practice milk steaming; making your two drinks sequentially fits this workflow.

The $729.95 Philips 3300 is the convenience alternative. Its matched Sur La Table page identifies LatteGo automatic milk frothing. As a general category expectation, a fully automatic bean-to-cup machine reduces hands-on preparation, although its milk system still needs cleaning. Choose it if that convenience is worth $80. Otherwise, I favor the Breville's lower price and hands-on control.

Buy one of these alternatives, not both. Neither calls for a separate grinder or frother. I reasonably expect normal operating accessories or built-in equivalents with these household machines, but the frozen evidence does not enumerate their complete accessory kits or electrical specifications. The page matches support the models, not independently verified seller fulfillment. The cards show aggregate merchant offers and 30-day returns; they do not establish every seller's terms.

candidates.evidence_and_reason: The explicitly identified Barista Express Impress supports an integrated espresso setup with grinding and milk steaming. Assisted tamping is a useful beginner feature under a model-knowledge assumption. Two sequential drinks fit its manual workflow. Target is identified without merchant aggregation, giving this offer slightly clearer seller attribution than the essentially same-priced Google alternative. It leaves $150.01 below budget.

Apparently the same Impress model and expected drink-making capabilities for four cents less. Whole Latte Love & more aggregates offers, so the actual seller at this price and applicable return terms are less clear. The negligible saving does not outweigh that modest uncertainty.

A credible fully automatic alternative within budget. Google's reported page match identifies LatteGo, supporting convenient milk preparation alongside bean-to-cup brewing. General category expectations favor less hands-on preparation but less espresso adjustment than a semiautomatic machine; cleaning remains necessary. Its $79.96 premium over the selected Breville is not compelling given willingness to steam manually, while aggregated seller attribution adds uncertainty.
Avoids spending and purchase risk, but credible complete setups within budget offer an acceptable prospect of satisfying the stated needs.
